ops.title: cc-transcript: shell-semantic Command normalization (unwrapped arity + executable dequoting)
ops.description:
The rm-guard adversarial review (2026-07-16) confirmed three parser-level gaps in `cc_transcript.command` that captain-hook consumers can only paper over locally:

1. **`Command.unwrapped` is not option-arity-aware.** `env -u HOME rm /x` unwraps to executable `HOME` with args `("rm", "/x")`; `sudo -u root rm /x` unwraps to `root`; `timeout 5s rm /x` unwraps to `5s` (bare ints are stripped, duration suffixes are not). Fix: per-wrapper option arity tables (at least `env -u/-C`, `sudo -u/-g/-p/-h`, `timeout` duration operand).
2. **`.executable` preserves shell quoting/escaping.** `\rm`, `'rm'`, `"rm"`, `/bin/\rm` all reach consumers with the quote/escape characters intact even though args are dequoted. `.executable` (or a parallel normalized accessor) should apply shell quote-removal semantics.
3. **Path arguments retain unquoted backslashes** (`..\/outside` vs bash's `../outside`) — same quote-removal pass should cover args consistently.

captain-hook's `packs/general/deletions.py` currently carries local normalization for (2)/(3) (dequote + unescape + casefold basename) and documents (1) as a known bypass (`env -u HOME rm`, `sudo -u root rm`, `timeout 5s rm` pass through the guard). When this lands upstream + the pin bumps, delete the local normalization and add dispatch tests for the wrapper spellings.

Refs: refuter findings 1-3 (blocker), finder findings 1/3 (major), rm-guard review 2026-07-16.

ops.text: Command.unwrapped consumes wrapper option operands (env -u/-C, sudo -u/-g, timeout durations) so the wrapped executable is recovered
Executable and args are shell-dequoted/unescaped consistently
captain-hook deletions.py local normalization removed after pin bump, with dispatch tests for the wrapper spellings
